key_observations: The manuscript moved from separate section notes toward a single coherent draft.
A figure-label inconsistency was corrected without changing the underlying experiment or evaluation protocol.
The discussion and contribution statement were narrowed to match the actual evidence, especially the limitation under distribution shift.
Unresolved claims were explicitly marked instead of being strengthened without supporting evidence.
The replication study did not re-enter the core workflow and remained appropriately parked.
priority_alignment: The day's main effort was aligned with the new post-experiment priority: manuscript completion.
Figure and citation cleanup supported the manuscript rather than expanding the experiment scope.
The brief unrelated browsing did not displace the majority of the day's research work.
important_uncertainty: Several marked claims still need either stronger wording or direct citation support.
The current draft may expose gaps in the methods-to-results narrative that were less visible when sections were separate.
The appropriate submission venue and exact deadline remain unresolved.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Complete a full read-through of the assembled draft from introduction through discussion, focusing on logical continuity and unsupported claims before adding any new research work.

primary_action.title: Do one end-to-end manuscript pass
primary_action.reason: The manuscript now exists as a single draft, so the highest-value next step is to identify structural gaps and unsupported claims before returning to optional experiments.

secondary_action.title: Keep the experimental scope frozen
secondary_action.reason: Today's work produced a coherent draft without needing new experiments; reopening the experimental loop now would interrupt manuscript consolidation.

things_not_to_do: Do not treat the corrected figure labels as evidence that the underlying experiment needs to be rerun.
Do not reopen the parked replication study during the manuscript consolidation pass.
Do not fill unresolved claims with stronger language merely to make the draft read more confidently.
